item.title: From the family
item.description: This is Cholpon. Our grandfather Jumabai Sydykov died on 11 September, at home, in his 80th year. He was buried the next day beside his father, under the apricot tree hill. He asked that the blog stay open, so that the poems are not lost with the notebook. Thank you to everyone who read him and…

item.title: The last lesson
item.description: My hands do not hold the komuz like before. I told my students on Wednesday: this is the last lesson. The girl with the loaf of bread (now fifteen) asked: "Ata, who will play the first string?" I said, "You." She did not answer. She played it. We drank tea. The father came to pick her up and I…

item.title: New Year
item.description: Eleven grandchildren came, and three great-grandchildren. The house was too small and the dog was too happy. Cholpon says there are 900 readers of this blog in six years. I said: that is one aitysh crowd. Good.

item.title: Autumn at seventy-eight
item.description: The year comes to me as to an old friend, without hurry, with a basket. Here is a quince, here is a first frost, here is a morning with nothing in it. I take them all and say thank you. A man of seventy-eight has room.

item.title: Sixty-one years
item.description: In May 1951 I wrote my first song, for a girl who didn't know my name. I was seventeen. Sixty-one years later I know the song, I know the girl's name, and I know why she didn't answer: she couldn't read. She is my wife. She learned to read from my letters. Cholpon says it's the best thing I have…

item.title: The song of the old tractor
item.description: A funny song for the New Year concert, in the style of the old tractor-station songs: Oh my Belarus, my iron brother, you ploughed this field for thirty years. You coughed, you stopped, you started again, you were like our mother-in-law. But you are rust now at the end of the field, and we all…

item.title: Grandfather's apricot
item.description: My father planted it in the year of the famine, when nobody planted anything. The neighbours laughed: who will eat it? Eighty years they have eaten it.

item.title: My friend the bee man
item.description: My friend keeps bees on the other side of the hill. His father and I were boys together; we stole apples together and we were punished together. Now the son keeps the bees, and the friendship came with the hives. He says bees are like akyns: they all sing at once and the honey is the result. On…

item.title: The singing box
item.description: My family gave me a telephone. It is small and grey and it plays a tune when someone calls. I do not like the tune. It is not a tune, it is a sneeze. Cholpon changed it to a komuz, but the komuz sounds like a toy. Last week it rang in the middle of the aitysh rehearsal. I answered. It was my…

item.title: The shepherd's wedding
item.description: A shepherd from the high pasture married a girl from the village last Saturday. They asked me for a song. I had none for a shepherd, so I made one at the table, between the lamb and the tea: You counted sheep, now count the days, the days are fewer than the sheep. But a day with her is a hundred…
